120	Why is this so important?	Por que isso é tão importante?
121	What is the story here?	Qual é a história?
122	So just to understand, or to build this up for a moment, because this is, after all, the soul of
	the Parashah — hmm, let me restate.
123	It touches each and every one of us, especially someone like me, past the age of 50.
124	Are there people in the audience past 50?
125	Good.
126	I want to take you into the verses we read, but with your permission, let's put on glasses of the past and try
127	to picture them.
128	Look, Abraham our father here is a hundred years old.
129	He is a hundred.
130	Now, he is a very, very, very distinguished man.
131	Very distinguished.
132	Everyone knows him, he is not anonymous at all.
133	He has already won the war of the four kings against the five, and made agreements with the king of
134	Sedom, and he is very wealthy, and Malki-Tzedek king of Shalem, all in the previous Parashah, brought out
135	for him bread and wine.
136	In the previous Parashah, yes.
137	He brings him bread and wine, and whether that Malki-Tzedek is Shem, Noah, or some other distinguished figure,
138	it is clear that he sees Abraham as a figure of admiration, and so on.
139	And afterward everyone gathers at the Valley of Shaveh; Rashi says the Valley of Shaveh, that they all sat to appoint Abraham
140	as their prince.
141	In the next Parashah, after Sarah died, the sons of Het say to Abraham, "You are a prince of God among us."
142	You are our prince, what do you mean?
143	Everyone knows you.
144	That is the situation.
145	Now picture this.
146	A distinguished man — and certainly the mitzvah of hospitality is important, but not to such a degree —
147	sees three men he does not know.
148	He runs and serves them like the lowliest
149	of servants.
150	How would you feel?
151	Imagine you came to Machon Meir and Rabbi Yaniv Hayun met you here at the entrance.
152	He tells you, "Ah, you've arrived at Machon Meir," and takes you by the hand, runs with you to the dining room, "Sit," runs, serves you
153	chicken, serves you salads, juice — "Sir, let me bring you" — and he stands there like that, "Anything else?"
154	Like a waiter, right?
155	We would die of embarrassment.
156	So what happened, people, what happened to Abraham?
157	Why does Abraham behave this way?
158	It is strange, odd behavior.
159	You, you have servants, you lack servants, you'd just do like this, snap.
